domain.name: cnv
domain.one_line: Censored newsvendor with Bayesian demand learning from stock-out timing (Jain, Rudi & Wang, Operations Research 2015).

demand.domain: integer >= 0: the number of customer arrivals in the unit-length period, Poisson(lambda) with the rate lambda unknown to the decision-maker — fixed for the horizon, prior Gamma(alpha, beta) in shape-rate form, never observed. The paper's general model admits any arrival process with independent stationary increments; the numerical study and this IR take the Poisson case
demand.source: paper §2 (general renewal setup) and §3/§5 (Poisson special case with the conjugate Gamma prior); the learning problem exists because lambda is never observed

epochs.domain: real in [0, 1], one per arrival: the arrival times within the period; given the count they are the order statistics of that many independent uniforms (the conditional-uniform representation of a Poisson process)
epochs.source: paper §2 (arrival epochs t^i of the demand process) and §3 (only the stock-out epoch matters under Poisson demand, Proposition 2)

order.domain: integer >= 0: the stocking level y set at the start of each period, delivered immediately
order.source: paper §2: the control; Proposition 1(c) gives a finite upper bound on the optimal level

sales.domain: integer in [0, order]: min(demand, order); unmet demand is lost and unobserved
sales.source: paper §2: lost sales, zero salvage, inventory delivered immediately

stockout_time.domain: real in [0, 1]: the arrival epoch of the last unit sold when a stock-out occurs, 1 when it does not, 0 when nothing was stocked
stockout_time.source: paper §3, the O^ST(y) observation: with Poisson demand this single number carries all the information in the sale epochs (Proposition 2(c))

r.domain: real > c: revenue per unit sold

c.domain: real in (0, r): cost per unit stocked
c.source: paper §2: stationary unit cost; the newsvendor ratio is (r - c) / r

out_of_scope: normal (Brownian-motion) demand: the paper's second special case; a second arrivals candidate could add it later without touching the skeleton
checkpoint observation models (paper §4): inventory observed only at predetermined times within a period
salvage value, holding cost, backlogging, lead times, fixed ordering cost: the paper's newsvendor is perishable with immediate delivery
discounting: the paper's objective is the undiscounted sum of expected profits
dynamics: episode start: lambda is drawn once from Gamma(alpha = beta * E[lambda], beta) and is never revealed

each period: the newsvendor stocks y units; the number of customers D arriving in the unit interval is Poisson(lambda), and given D their arrival epochs are D independent uniforms on [0, 1] (the conditional-uniform representation of a Poisson process)
sales = min(D, y); a stock-out occurs when D >= y; the stock-out time is the arrival epoch of the y-th customer when D >= y >= 1, 0 when y = 0, and 1 when no stock-out occurs
the running totals S <- S + sales and T <- T + stock-out time are the paper's sufficient statistic under timing observations (Proposition 2(b)); D_cum <- D_cum + D is the full-observation counterpart
profit[t] = r * sales - c * y; maximize the expected undiscounted sum over t in 0..N-1

notation.y: stocking level (order) placed at the start of a period
notation.D: demand: number of arrivals in the period
notation.t^s: stock-out time: arrival epoch of the last unit sold
notation.alpha, beta: Gamma prior shape and rate on lambda; posterior under timing is Gamma(alpha + S, beta + T)
notation.S, T: cumulative sales and cumulative sales duration (paper's script S and script T)
notation.y^M: myopic (single-period newsvendor) stocking level under the current posterior
notation.lambda: the unknown Poisson arrival rate, the demand quantity's hidden parameter; posterior under timing is Gamma(alpha + S, beta + T)

state_variables.name: period
state_variables.desc: current period t; horizon ends when period == horizon_N

state_variables.name: cum_sales
state_variables.desc: cumulative sales S over the periods played so far: the first coordinate of the timing-observation sufficient statistic (posterior shape = prior shape + S)

state_variables.name: cum_duration
state_variables.desc: cumulative sales duration T: one full period when no stock-out occurred, the stock-out time otherwise; second coordinate of the timing statistic (posterior rate = prior rate + T)

state_variables.name: cum_demand
state_variables.desc: cumulative realized demand: the full-observation sufficient statistic (posterior shape = prior shape + cum_demand, rate = prior rate + periods played). Carried by the simulator so the full_belief mode can render it; it is never read by a transition

info_fields.name: demand
info_fields.desc: arrivals in the period; observed by the agent only under the full observation type

placement.rationale: no later transition reads it; the cumulative total the full_belief mode needs is a state variable of its own

info_fields.name: stockout_event
info_fields.desc: 1 when demand >= order (all stock sold), else 0

info_fields.name: stockout_time
info_fields.desc: arrival epoch of the last unit sold when a stock-out occurs; 0.0 when order == 0; 1.0 when no stock-out

info_fields.name: action_period
info_fields.desc: period the emitting decision was taken (boundary invariant)

decisions.name: order

type.rationale: the paper's stocking level y is an integer count of units sold to unit-sized Poisson arrivals

bounds.rationale: stock beyond the number of arrival epochs the simulator holds in one period (arrivals_buffer, also the demand cap) can never sell, so the buffer length is the model's own cap on any useful order; it is derived from the marginal demand law of the widest grid cell, never from a solved policy

decisions.desc: stocking level y placed at the start of the period, delivered immediately

updates: stockout_time = 0.0 if order == 0 else (topk(u[:demand], demand - order + 1)[-1] if demand >= order else 1.0)

per_step_components.name: stocking
per_step_components.desc: -c * y: the stocking cost, negative so components sum to profit

invariants.name: sales_are_censored_demand
invariants.desc: you sell what arrives, up to what you stocked; the rest is lost

invariants.name: demand_within_buffer
invariants.desc: the simulator cannot generate more arrivals than its buffer

invariants.name: stockout_iff_all_sold
invariants.desc: a stock-out is exactly the event that every stocked unit sold

invariants.name: stockout_time_in_period
invariants.desc: the stock-out time is an epoch inside the unit period

invariants.name: no_stockout_means_full_duration
invariants.desc: without a stock-out the newsvendor observed sales for the whole period

invariants.name: zero_stock_means_zero_duration
invariants.desc: stocking nothing yields no sales duration and no information

invariants.name: cum_sales_balance
invariants.desc: the sales total moves only by this period's sales

invariants.name: cum_duration_balance
invariants.desc: the duration total moves only by this period's sales duration

invariants.name: cum_demand_balance
invariants.desc: the demand total moves only by this period's demand

invariants.name: profit_identity
invariants.desc: profit is revenue on sales less the cost of everything stocked

constants.name: horizon_N
constants.desc: ordering periods N: 4 for the paper's exact-DP study (§5.1), 100 for the myopic-policy simulation (§5.3, fig6a/fig6b)

constants.name: price
constants.desc: revenue r per unit sold; fixed at 2 throughout the paper's study

constants.name: unit_cost
constants.desc: cost c per unit stocked; the paper sweeps 0.2..1.8 in steps of 0.1 (newsvendor ratio 0.9..0.1)

constants.name: prior_rate
constants.desc: Gamma rate beta of the prior on lambda; the paper sweeps 1/beta in {0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16} (the scale parameter, the degree of demand uncertainty)

constants.name: prior_mean
constants.desc: prior expected arrival rate E[lambda] = alpha / beta; the paper sweeps {10, 20, 30, 40, 50}. Prior shape alpha = prior_rate * prior_mean

constants.name: arrivals_buffer
constants.desc: uniform epochs drawn per period, also the demand cap: 402 is the 1e-8 upper quantile of the marginal (negative-binomial) per-period demand of the widest grid cell (1/beta = 16, E[lambda] = 50); every other cell's tail is smaller. A model-derived envelope, never a measurement of a solved policy

uncertainty_slots.name: demand

poisson.desc: Poisson(lambda) arrivals per unit period with the hidden per-episode rate lambda ~ Gamma(alpha, beta) drawn once (the conjugate prior); the count of a Poisson process on [0, 1]

uncertainty_slots.desc: the number of customer arrivals in a period

uncertainty_slots.name: epochs

uniform.desc: arrivals_buffer i.i.d. uniform epochs on [0, 1]; conditional on the count D, the first D of them (unordered) are the arrival epochs of a Poisson process on the unit interval, and their order statistics are the arrival times

uncertainty_slots.desc: where in the period the arrivals fall

expr_builtins.name: poisson_quantile
expr_builtins.desc: smallest integer y with P(Poisson(rate) <= y) >= q: the newsvendor quantity under a known rate

observation_modes.name: timing_belief
observation_modes.desc: the paper's timing model as a Markov state: the Gamma posterior (shape, rate) after conjugate updating on sales and stock-out times, plus the cost regime and the clock. Replicates the paper's solution structure; no memory needed

observation_modes.name: full_belief
observation_modes.desc: the full-observation model as a Markov state: posterior after seeing every arrival (shape + cum_demand, rate + periods played)

observation_modes.name: event_raw
observation_modes.desc: the paper's event observation O^E = (sales, stock-out flag) for the last period, plus the prior and cost regime; the policy must carry its own memory (frame stack over the horizon). No fixed-size sufficient statistic exists for this type, so raw is its only encoding

observation_modes.name: timing_raw
observation_modes.desc: the paper's stock-out timing observation O^ST = (sales, stock-out time) for the last period, plus the prior and cost regime; memory via frame stack. The bypass arm against timing_belief

observation_modes.name: full_raw
observation_modes.desc: the full observation O^F: last period's demand including lost sales, plus the prior and cost regime; memory via frame stack. The bypass arm against full_belief

observation_modes.name: timing_belief_ctx
observation_modes.desc: timing_belief plus the prior's own parameters (rate, mean): the belief already folds the prior in, but a GENERALIST over the paper510 grid conditions on the cell explicitly — the grid's axes are unit_cost (via the critical ratio, price fixed), prior_rate and prior_mean, so every axis is in the vector

observation_modes.name: full_belief_ctx
observation_modes.desc: full_belief plus the prior's parameters (rate, mean), for the generalist — see timing_belief_ctx

observation_modes.name: full_belief_log
observation_modes.desc: full_belief's sufficient statistic recoded as (log posterior mean, posterior CV) — a bijection of (post_shape, post_rate) in a scale the network can resolve: under standardised (shape, rate) the period-0/1 states that need orders 0, 10 and 28 sit 0.03 apart (#E56); here 1.7-4.5 apart

observation_modes.name: full_belief_ms
observation_modes.desc: full_belief's sufficient statistic recoded as (posterior mean, posterior sd), no log — the coordinate change of full_belief_log without its log (#E63): a bijection of (post_shape, post_rate)

observation_modes.name: timing_belief_log
observation_modes.desc: timing_belief's sufficient statistic recoded as (log posterior mean, posterior CV) — the #E59 recoding applied to the timing posterior (shape = prior + cum_sales, rate = prior + cum_duration); a bijection of (post_shape, post_rate)

action_modes.name: order_discrete
action_modes.desc: identity encoding over integer stocking levels 0..arrivals_buffer

reward_modes.name: profit
reward_modes.desc: per-period profit r * sales - c * order; the objective itself, undiscounted

requires_memory.rationale: the hidden per-episode rate must be inferred from censored observations; the *_raw modes carry only the last period and rely on a frame stack over the horizon, while the *_belief modes carry the conjugate posterior and are Markov on their own (frame_stack 1 at launch)

obs_normalization.rationale: posterior shape and rate, sales and the cost ratio differ by two orders of magnitude across the grid; spec §8.3 says normalize

eval_metrics.name: hindsight_profit
eval_metrics.desc: profit of a clairvoyant who stocks exactly this period's demand; the regret denominator the legacy scripts called profit_max. Describes, never decides
eval_metrics.source: legacy cnv eval column (regret_mean); kept as a report-only column

eval_metrics.name: perfect_profit
eval_metrics.expr: price * min(demand, poisson_quantile(demand_rate, (price - unit_cost) / price)) - unit_cost * poisson_quantile(demand_rate, (price - unit_cost) / price)
eval_metrics.desc: profit of the paper's perfect-knowledge model P: knows lambda and stocks the Poisson newsvendor quantity every period. Reads the hidden rate, which a metric may. Describes, never decides
eval_metrics.source: paper §5.3, the benchmark with perfect knowledge of the demand distribution

benchmarks.name: myopic
benchmarks.basis: the paper's myopic policies (§5.3): each period stock the single-period newsvendor quantity under the current posterior. timing: Gamma(alpha + S, beta + T) via the conjugate update (7); full: Gamma(alpha + cum_demand, beta + n); event: no conjugate prior, posterior by brute-force likelihood (4) over the history — feasible at N=4 only

benchmarks.name: dp
benchmarks.basis: backward induction of the paper's dynamic program (3) over the belief state at N=4: exact over the integer lattice (shape) for the full type; for the timing type the rate coordinate is continuous and is discretized, with the grid recorded as the numerical basis at build. The event-type optimum needs the full history and is not attempted

benchmarks.name: perfect
benchmarks.basis: clairvoyant: reads the realized lambda and stocks the Poisson newsvendor quantity; the paper's model P, the ceiling every learning model is measured against

benchmarks.name: random
benchmarks.basis: the spec-§8.6 floors: `uniform` draws the stocking level uniformly over the action space on a policy stream; `prior_mean` stocks round(E[lambda]) every period and never learns. Build diagnostics, never escalation triggers

tier2.structure: over-ordering: the optimal stocking level under censored observations exceeds the myopic newsvendor level y^M (Proposition 1(b)), by less under timing than under event observations in most of the grid (§5.1, Figure 3)
tier2.claim: the trained belief-fed policies stock above the myopic level as a function of the posterior, and the timing policy's excess is smaller than the event policy's
tier2.instrument: cnv_policy_probe.py: sweep the learned order over posterior (shape, rate) x critical ratio against the myopic and DP quantities; action agreement with the DP; paired scoring of the fitted rule

tier2.structure: the two-number sufficient statistic (cumulative sales, cumulative sales duration) of Proposition 2
tier2.claim: a policy fed only raw per-period observations with a frame stack (timing_raw) matches the profit of the policy fed the statistic (timing_belief), so the conjugate machinery need not be handed over; likewise full_raw vs full_belief
tier2.instrument: paired observation-mode contrast on shared seed blocks, per grid cell

grids.name: paper510
grids.desc: the paper's §5.1 study: 17 unit costs (newsvendor ratio 0.1..0.9) x 6 prior scales (1/beta in 0.5..16) x 5 prior means (10..50) = 510 cells at N = 4. The primary generalist target: one policy per observation type trained on cells sampled uniformly, evaluated per cell against the cell's own DP and myopic bars

grids.name: fig3
grids.desc: the paper's Figures 3(a) and 4(a): the unit-cost sweep at alpha = 10/16, beta = 1/16 (E[lambda] = 10, 1/beta = 16), 17 cells at N = 4

assumptions_log: The arrival process is simulated by the conditional-uniform method (human-chosen over summed exponential gaps, which the catalog form cannot parameterise by rate, and over the equivalent Beta order-statistic shortcut): demand ~ Poisson(lambda), then arrivals_buffer = 402 i.i.d. uniform epochs of which the first `demand` are the arrival epochs. Demand is capped at the buffer, the 1e-8 marginal-demand quantile of the widest grid cell. The legacy simulator's exponential-gap buffer (26..86) capped demand materially in the diffuse-prior cells.
Stocking level is an integer in [0, arrivals_buffer]; the upper bound is the simulator's own arrival cap, not a fact about the problem (Proposition 1(c) only says the optimum is finite).

Observation types are gym observation modes, not scenario modes: event_raw / timing_raw / full_raw carry the last period only (frame stack over the horizon supplies memory); timing_belief / full_belief carry the conjugate posterior computed from the state's running totals. Dropped from the legacy folder: the 'sales' mode (informationally identical to event) and the per-step regret and terminal gap reward modes (the per-step one leaks demand to a memory policy; the terminal one can return as a gym-layer lever).

The running totals cum_sales, cum_duration, cum_demand live in the state although no transition reads them: they are carried so the belief modes can render the paper's sufficient statistic (the mab example's pulls/payouts precedent).
When order == 0 the period yields sales 0, stock-out event 1 and stock-out time 0, so the timing posterior is unchanged (beta + 0), as in the paper's equation (7).
Period indexing 0-based; horizon_N = 4 (the DP study) with 100 for the fig6 instances; horizon end is `terminated`.

Seed scheme v2: the demand slot draws on stream 0 and the epochs slot on stream 1 each period; the hidden rate lambda is the demand slot's world latent, drawn once per episode on meta substream 0 (desugared placeholder constant demand_rate).
